title: Mars propellant production at mission scale
bottleneck: Making methane and oxygen propellant on Mars via the Sabatier reaction plus water electrolysis is proven chemistry — MOXIE made oxygen on Mars in 2021 — but scaling from grams to the 500-plus tons needed for a Starship return is a four-order-of-magnitude jump. It requires finding and extracting subsurface water ice at the landing site, a megawatt-scale power source running for about two years, autonomous plant operation, and cryogenic liquefaction and storage of the product. No integrated system has been built even on Earth.
why_it_blocks: Starship-class Mars return is impossible without refueling on Mars; the propellant plant is the long pole of the entire Mars architecture, and it must work before the crew leaves Earth.
current_state: MOXIE (oxygen only, grams) succeeded; full-scale plant designs exist on paper in NASA's Design Reference Architecture. No pilot plant and no Martian water extraction demo exist.
